Massa polmonare in un paziente anziano:: Lung mass in an elderly patient: contrast-enhanced chest CT (and upper abdomen) to characterise and stage it, then histological diagnosis
Un'opacità polmonare oltre i 3 cm è una: A lung opacity larger than 3 cm is a mass: in an adult or elderly smoker it should be considered a tumour until proven otherwise. The X-ray shows where it is, but that is not enough: contrast-enhanced CT characterises it (margins, cavitation, relationship with mediastinum and chest wall), looks for lymph nodes and metastases and guides biopsy. A pneumonia can resemble a mass: if antibiotics are chosen, a follow-up X-ray after 6-8 weeks is mandatory, because a «pneumonia that does not resolve» may hide a tumour. Always also look for rib erosion, effusion and an elevated diaphragm (phrenic nerve palsy).
Oltre 3 cm è una massa: TC con mezzo di: Over 3 cm it is a mass: contrast-enhanced CT and histology; do not stop at antibiotics.
